summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive scrollytelling website that tells the stories of five NASA machines left behind on the Moon and Mars: the Apollo 11 lunar module "Eagle", the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, and the Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity, plus the Ingenuity helicopter. Using real NASA mission data and photos, each machine gets a short, easy-to-read story with key facts such as location, shape, mass, and current status. We use everyday comparisons, like a two-layer cake with legs or shoes meant for 3 months that last 14 years, so anyone can understand complex space missions. The project matters because it makes space history and exploration engaging for students and the general public, and it reminds people that these machines still sit on other worlds. All data and image credits go to NASA.
details: What it does: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive scrollytelling website about five NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars: the Apollo 11 lunar module "Eagle", the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Spirit, Opportunity, and the Ingenuity helicopter. A rocket countdown opens the page, then each machine gets its own story card with a real NASA photo and key facts (location, shape, mass, status). A moving banner and a "next" teaser keep readers scrolling. Benefits and impact: Space history becomes easy to remember and fun to read. Students, kids, and beginners can enjoy NASA missions without technical background, and free NASA data becomes a story anyone can share. Tools: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, hosted on Netlify. Photos come from the NASA Image and Video Library (images.nasa.gov), and facts are based on NASA mission information. Photo credits are listed in the demo. Story text and some code were made with help from Claude, an AI assistant. Creativity: We turn technical mission data into short stories using everyday comparisons, such as a two-layer cake with legs for the lunar module, or shoes meant for 3 months that last 14 years for Opportunity. Factors considered: Accuracy (numbers marked "about" are estimates), simple language for all ages, proper NASA credits, and a fast, mobile-friendly design.
